L1@P0: On the Chabauty space of locally compact abelian groups
L2@P0: YVES CORNULIER
L3@P0: This paper contains several results about the Chabauty space of a general locally compact abelian group. Notably, we determine its topological dimension, we characterize
L4@P0: when it is totally disconnected or connected; we characterize isolated points.

L6@P0: 1 Introduction
L7@P0: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space. The set F.X/ of closed subsets can
L8@P0: be endowed with the Chabauty topology, which makes it a compact Hausdorff space.
L9@P0: For this topology, a net .Yi/ converges to Y if and only if .Yi [ f1g/ converges to
L10@P0: Y [ f1g in the Hausdorff topology of the one-point compactification of X . When
L11@P0: X is second countable, F.X/ is metrizable. See details in Section 2.1. If G is a
L12@P0: locally compact group, the set S.G/ of closed subgroups of G is closed in F.G/ and
L13@P0: therefore is compact Hausdorff as well.
L14@P0: Introduced by Chabauty in [7], the Chabauty topology has been studied by Hubbard and
L15@P0: Pourezza [24], Protasov [25], Protasov and Tsybenko [27; 26], Fisher and Gartside [13;
L16@P0: 14], Bridson, de la Harpe and Kleptsyn [6], Kloeckner [20], Haettel [16], and more
L17@P0: specifically for discrete groups by Grigorchuk [15], Champetier [8], and by the author
L18@P0: together with Guyot and Pitsch [9; 10]. The fine study of S.G/ is subtle even for
L19@P0: apparently simple examples. While it is readily seen that S.R/ is homeomorphic to
L20@P0: a segment, a tricky argument due to Hubbard and Pourezza [24] shows that S.R2/
L21@P0: is homeomorphic to the 4-sphere. For n  3, S.Rn/ is known to be singular (that
L22@P0: is, not a topological manifold, even with boundary) but Kloeckner [20] showed that
L23@P0: S.Rn/ has a natural “stratification" which in particular makes it a simply connected and
L24@P0: locally contractible space; however S.Rn/ has not yet unveiled all its mysteries and for
L25@P0: instance it is still unknown whether it can be triangulated. Besides, Haettel [16] gave a
L26@P0: full description of the space S.R  Z/, showing in particular that it is path-connected
L27@P0: but not locally connected, and has uncountable fundamental group.

L108@P3: itself, while in the second case S.G/ is not totally disconnected by Theorem 1.5. Note

L113@P3: The next result concerns isolated points. When G is a discrete abelian group, a
L114@P3: necessary and sufficient condition for a subgroup H to be isolated in S.G/ is that H
L115@P3: is isolated in S.H/ and f1g is isolated in S.G=H/ (see for instance the paper [10] by
L116@P3: the author, Guyot and Pitsch). However when G is not assumed discrete, this condition
L117@P3: obviously remains necessary but is not sufficient: for instance Z is not isolated in
L118@P3: S.R/. The characterization of isolated points goes as follows (we refer to Section 2.4
L119@P3: for the definition of Artinian and adic groups)
L120@P3: Theorem 1.7 Let G be an LCA-group and H a closed subgroup. Then H is an
L121@P3: isolated point in S.G/ if and only if we are in one of the two (dual to each other) cases
L122@P3: (1) H ' A P , G=H ' D, A finitely generated abelian, P adic, D Artinian (so
L123@P3: G is totally disconnected);
L124@P3: (2) H ' P , G=H ' T  D, P adic, T torus, D Artinian (so G is elliptic).
L125@P3: In [10], the study was pursued to a complete description of the homeomorphism type
L126@P3: of S.G/, when G is a countable discrete abelian group. It would be interesting to
L127@P3: generalize this to second countable, totally disconnected LCA-groups. Among those
L128@P3: groups, those for which this question is nontrivial have a very special form: they have
L129@P3: to lie in an exact sequence

L131@P3: with A, P , D as in Theorem 1.7(1), since if G is not of this form, by the same
L132@P3: theorem, S.G/ has no isolated point and therefore is a Cantor space.

L139@P4: This section recalls definitions and basic results used throughout the paper.
L140@P4: 2.1 The Chabauty topology
L141@P4: Recall that if X is a locally compact space, we denote by F.X/ the set of closed
L142@P4: subsets of X . This set has several natural topologies. The one of interest for us is
L143@P4: called the Chabauty topology (or compact topology), and is compact Hausdorff. It
L144@P4: appears in an exercise by Bourbaki [2, Chapitre 8, Section 5] and was reintroduced by
L145@P4: Narens [22] in the context and language of non-standard analysis and its description in
L146@P4: standard terms was then provided by Wattenberg [29]. Given a compact subset K  X
L147@P4: and open subsets U1; : : : ; Uk  X , define
